note: One film per lecture, in the order of the contents page. No time cap: every section of each lecture gets a chapter. Every film opens on the shared journey chart, marking where this lecture sits on the route. Chapter rows: [id, style, title, what it covers].

films.title: The Land of the Light Spiritual
films.lecture: First Public Lecture in the East (Colombo)
chapters: The ship reaches Ceylon on 15 January 1897; the whole route of the tour ahead is laid out.
The Hindus of Colombo present their address; the Swami credits India's support for his Western work.
India as the land of introspection and spirituality, the blessed land of Karma.
Ideas carried by Greek battalions and the Roman Eagle, against ideas carried by blessing: never fire and sword.
A spider's web on the Capitol
Empires come and go; the Capitoline ruins under a spider's web. Political greatness is never the mission of this race.
Religion is the centre of Indian life, down to the labourer with a mark on his forehead.
India stores spiritual energy and releases it; her gift to the world is the light spiritual.
Indian thought wins by fascination, slow and silent as the morning dew, not by force.
Modern learning shatters crude theologies; Vedanta offers a broader view of God and the soul.
Eternal principles stand while customs rightly change from Yuga to Yuga; Manu and the Smritis.
Baal, Moloch and Yahveh fight for their tribes; the Vedic Rishis go another way.
"That which exists is One; sages call It by various names."
The Mahimnah-stotra: many rivers, one sea. India builds temples for Mohammedans and Christians.
India's mission: mildness, forbearance and brotherhood, taught to every race and creed.

films.title: Vaidika: The Common Ground
films.lecture: Vedantism
chapters: The chief centre of Hinduism in Ceylon; the evening after the address of welcome.
A name that lost its meaning
"Hindu" comes from Sindhu; he prefers Vaidika or Vedantist.
The Vedas are eternal knowledge; the Rishis are Mantra-drashtas, discoverers of what already is.
Karma Kanda and Jnana Kanda; the Upanishads are what every sect must accept.
Human books that change with society; the Puranas teach philosophy through stories.
Nature has no beginning; cycles of projection and Pralaya. Parallel: Lavoisier's conservation of mass, 1789.
God is not partial: the rain falls on all fields, and the cultivated one bears fruit.
Souls are eternal and Karma shapes each life: we alone are responsible for what we suffer.
The Self is not the mind, and is the same in all beings: the basis of brotherhood.
Heavens are temporary, as Nahusha's fall from Indra's throne shows; Mukti is the goal.
The Personal God, and the Impersonal Absolute of the Advaita.
Ethics from oneness; strength: "Whatever you think, that you will be."
Variety is the soul of life
Every Ishta is a path; the moment you quarrel you are going back towards the brutes.
Castes and institutions have protected the nation; keep them until they die a natural death.
Dana is the duty of the Kali Yuga; first learn to obey, and command will come by itself.

films.title: Never Passive
films.lecture: Reply to the Address of Welcome at Pamban
chapters: First landing in India; the Raja of Ramnad greets him; the address under a decorated pandal.
The sacred motherland of philosophy, of Rishis and of renunciation.
"I discard the idea that India was ever passive": her activity is in religion.
A shoemaker and a bricklayer each see only their own trade; outsiders misjudge India the same way.
Vibrations too intense to be seen; the yogi sees past the material veil. Parallel: Ritter's ultraviolet, 1801.
Others trace their descent from robber-barons in fortresses; Hindus from Rishis in caves.
Krishna's teaching: the Lord is the Lord of all religions, an idea that belongs to India.
No salvation except by conquering desire; no one is free who is bound to matter.
Degraded now, yet we can become great; thanks to the Raja who first sent him to Chicago.

films.title: Real Worship
films.lecture: Address at the Rameswaram Temple on Real Worship
chapters: The people gathered at the temple ask the Swami to speak.
Religion is in love, not ceremony; outer worship is only a symbol of the inner.
Holy places do not cancel sin; a place is holy because of holy people.
He who sees Shiva in the poor, the weak and the diseased really worships Shiva.
One praises the master's face and dances; the other tends the garden and the master's children.
Service brings chitta-shuddhi; on a clean mirror the Shiva within shows.
Selfishness is the chief sin; "I will even go to hell if by doing so I can help my brothers."

films.title: The Giant Rising
films.lecture: Reply to the Address of Welcome at Ramnad
chapters: 25 January 1897: the first Indian territory reached on his return.
The long night ends; a breeze from the Himalayas; the giant rises to her feet.
The Raja of Ramnad first inspired the mission to Chicago.
Not politics or wealth: spirituality is the foundation of Indian life.
Pravritti and Nivritti; renunciation is the watchword of the Indian religions.
A thirsty man drinks from a ditch beside a fountain; the universe as a mud-puddle.
Let the poor enjoy a little first; renunciation comes by degrees, not by rules forced on all.
Rooted orthodoxy over shallow imitation; learn from every nation, assimilate what is of use.
"If there is any sin in the world, it is weakness."
Each life has a mission from its past Karma; other pursuits are harmony around one theme.
Mushroom nations rise and melt; a nation that drops its spiritual core dies within three generations.
Nowhere else was the idea of God so fully developed: the prayer of many names.
"Let us all work hard, my brethren; this is no time for sleep."

films.title: Strength Is Goodness
films.lecture: Reply to the Address of Welcome at Paramakudi
chapters: The first stop after Ramnad; a public demonstration; his Western disciples with him.
His love for his countrymen does not depend on how they receive him.
Civilisations swing between spirit and matter, and each swing brings its own excess.
Western political systems failing; wealth gathered by a few.
East and West correct each other's excesses; no single people saves the world.
Without a spiritual foundation, Western civilisation will crumble within fifty years.
The Atman shared by Hindus, Jains and Buddhists; only Avidya separates man from God.
Seen as one, the world becomes a play, however terrible it appears.
What I have done, I can undo
Karma made this body; each of us is heir-apparent to the Emperor of emperors.
Advaita meets the devotee and the rationalist alike, and must underlie the new society.

films.title: Bring It Out
films.lecture: Reply to the Address of Welcome at Shivaganga and Manamadura
chapters: The zemindars and citizens present their address.
He is not up to a long speech; the mountain and Mohammed.
An empire on which the sun never sets, against rule over the mind. India is still living.
Nothing can injure us unless we first injure ourselves. Parallel: germ theory and the healthy host (Koch, 1882).
Those who left for other faiths: it was a good deal our own fault.
"Our God is the cooking-pot, and our religion is, Don't touch me, I am holy."
Spiritual life first, then secular knowledge, then life, then food.
Bring the treasure out; twenty-five years of work; life subordinated to one high ideal.

films.title: Essentials and Non-essentials
films.lecture: Reply to the Address of Welcome at Madura
chapters: Three weeks of travel; the city of Sundareshwara; the Hindu public's address.
A short reply; the Raja of Ramnad's part in Chicago.
Persia, Greece, England: each age India gave spirituality to the rising power.
Revival can turn into fanaticism; materialism waits on the other side. We cannot become Western.
The Southern Brahmin's horror of meat; the Northern goat sacrifice; bullocks once killed for guests.
The Vedas are eternal; Smritis and Puranas belong to their time.
Reform by blessing and replacing, not by cursing.
Rishihood: religion experienced directly; a heart deep as the ocean, broad as the skies.

films.title: The Mission of the Vedanta
films.lecture: The Mission of the Vedanta
chapters: Two addresses, from the Hindu community and the students.
Even peasants followed news of the Parliament of Religions.
From the Ganga's icy bed, the current runs where it must; a great tree cannot be transplanted.
Western religion as an ornament; here, God alone is true and the world is fleeting.
India has endured for millennia without conquering anyone.
Dr Barrows' claim for Christianity; why Vedanta can be the universal religion.
Avatars and the Ishta illustrate the principles; they are not the foundation.
Vedanta inward, science outward, reach the same unity. Parallel: conservation of energy (Helmholtz, 1847).
Babylonian and Jewish tribal gods bred bloodshed; one truth, many names bred toleration.
One Existence throughout the universe: the rational basis of ethics.
Faith in ourselves and in God is the secret of greatness; dualist and Advaitist alike.
Our own responsibility for the oppression of the poor; arguments from heredity rejected.
Cursing and imitation have failed; grow along national lines with love.
Spiritual wisdom and renunciation as the goal for all: the Vedantic answer to caste.
"Arise, awake": carry Vedanta to every door.

films.title: From the Carriage Box
films.lecture: Reply to the Address of Welcome at Madras
chapters: The reception committee's address; the Maharaja of Khetri's address read aloud.
Harmony among religions; hope for an end to bigotry.
The hall gives way to a crowd; he speaks from a carriage. Man proposes, God disposes.
Religion is the bed-rock here; elsewhere a minor occupation.
Ceylon villagers knew nothing of European politics, yet knew of Chicago.
Renunciation, fearlessness and love against competition, cruel, cold and heartless.
Caste as the breaking of competition and the mitigation of its cruelties.
The crowd surges; he asks them to keep the fire burning.

films.title: My Plan of Campaign
films.lecture: My Plan of Campaign
chapters: Four years since he left from here; three years of silence abroad.
Ready now to answer the misunderstandings, caring little for the reaction.
Honour to Mrs Besant's work, but no help in America, and why he will not join.
Missionaries, and a countryman leading a reform party, worked against him.
His caste answered; any of the twice-born may take Sannyasa.
Madras's steady growth against Bengal's reactions; "I believe in growth."
Evil moves from limb to limb; a wave needs a hollow; fanatical reform defeats itself.
The drowning boy who asks to be pulled out before the lecture.
Without an educated public, law changes nothing; the tyranny of a minority.
Buddhism's decline; Shankara, Ramanuja, Nanak, Chaitanya, Kabir, Dadu built on tradition.
Each nation has its vital centre; India's is religion. Spiritual ideas first.
The highest gift; India's thought once reached China, Asia Minor, the Malay archipelago.
Train young men as preachers; a man-making religion; no weakening mysticism.
Patriotism: feel, find the way, and will; the squirrel's sand on Rama's bridge.
Society is a leaking ship; never let curses rise to our lips.

films.title: Strength from Every Page
films.lecture: Vedanta in its Application to Indian Life
chapters: The name and the river; Vedanta as the name for all Indian religious life.
Shruti over Smriti; local practice is mostly Puranic; the Sama-Veda's lost thousand branches.
Commentators bend texts to their school; Ajā as unborn, or as she-goat.
Dvaita, Vishishtadvaita, Advaita are steps on one road.
The Upanishads seek the infinite within, where other poetry seeks it in muscle and storm.
Two birds on one tree: one eats the fruit, one looks on in glory.
Strength on every page: the sannyasin who would not go to Greece.
The queen sings to her baby: thou art the pure, the stainless.
The soul is already perfect; evolution is the widening of the hole, not change in what is behind.
The world moving towards unity. Parallel: Maxwell unites electricity, magnetism and light, 1865.
Physical weakness is the cause; strength before scripture.
Caste as natural grouping may stay; privilege must end.
Look upon everyone as God; you cannot help anyone, you can only serve.

films.title: The Sages of India
films.lecture: The Sages of India
chapters: Countless sages; a few who made epochs.
Shrutis eternal; Smritis and Puranas yield when they conflict.
Religions built on one person rise and fall with that person's history.
The Rishi perceives spiritual truth as directly as we perceive a table.
Religion is not in books or talk; the son whose face shines with Brahman.
The ideal king, son and husband.
Unique, depicted once and for all; she is in the vitals of the race.
Work for its own sake; the love of the Gopis, defended.
Teacher of the poor; later decline; the Jagannath temple.
Intellect, breadth and heart, across the map of India.
Head and heart joined; any truth here is his, any error mine.

films.title: The Work Before Us
films.lecture: The Work Before Us
chapters: Fourteen years of wandering; the problem must be seen whole.
Ideas must widen to cover humanity.
Environment turned the Indian mind within and the Greek mind outward.
Art, music and religion lost originality; scholars argued over touch and ritual.
Benefits without new vigour; the link with Greek-derived Europe.
Each nation must give in order to live; wisdom does not march upon bleeding bodies.
Anonymous authors; thought spreading like dew.
Roman and English roads carry ideas; a spiritual conquest of the world.
Materialism and superstition; avoid all mystery.
Principles over persons; texts for every stage.
The Sufi at the closed door; the Gopis who became Krishna.
Stand up and express the divinity within you.

films.title: The Future of India
films.lecture: The Future of India
chapters: Tidal waves of spirituality flowing outward from India.
The fallen fruit decays and feeds the new tree.
Race, religion, language and government: a harder problem than any nation's.
Religion is the only unifying base; make it known everywhere.
Temples destroyed and rebuilt; culture withstands shocks, not mere knowledge.
Teach through the vernaculars; spread Sanskrit learning too.
Theories of separate races and of Aryans from outside, disputed.
Raise the lower castes; the Brahmin like the cobra drawing out its own poison.
The ass that knows its load's weight, not its worth; acquire Sanskrit culture.
A handful of Japanese, a few English: the secret is organisation.
The Vedic verse: the gods, being of one mind, received the oblations.
Worship your countrymen as the living God.
A non-sectarian temple, and training for teachers.
Information without character produces nothing original.
Give your energy to the nation and to one great ideal.

films.title: On Charity
films.lecture: On Charity
chapters: At the annual meeting he answers a speaker who objected to alms for Brahmins.
Take away the means that let them think, and the whole nation suffers.
Western discriminate charity: police, courts and prisons; beggars turned into criminals.
Poverty lasts as long as civilisation does; Indian giving has its good side as well as its bad.

films.title: I Am Your Brother
films.lecture: Address of Welcome Presented at Calcutta and Reply
chapters: A week after arrival; Raja Radha Kanta Deb's house; Raja Benoy Krishna presides.
Chicago, London, the simple life, and Ramakrishna.
He returns not as a sannyasin but as a brother.
The Parliament was an opening, not the purpose.
American hospitality; his love for the English; work in England that will last.
Here alone poverty does not mean crime.
All good is his; the faults are mine.
The Gita's promise; the upheaval now under way.
Every part of national life must rest on religion.
Give spirituality, take science; Raja Rammohan Roy began it.
The oyster in its shell will not do.
Three days at the house of Death: Shraddha, faith in oneself.
Young men of Calcutta: be fearless and carry the work.

films.title: The Vedanta in All Its Phases
films.lecture: The Vedanta in all its phases
chapters: The oldest teaching, and the last word.
To Athens, Alexandria and Antioch; Sankhya and the other systems.
Every sect, dualist or monist, appeals to the Upanishads.
Two commentators, Bodhayana before them, Vyasa's Sutras above.
The Gita next in authority; spurious texts like the Allopanishad.
The poetry of the Upanishads turns from the outer sky to the Atman.
Village custom and Vamachara have displaced the Upanishads.
Power is already within; the farmer breaks the mud-wall and the water flows.
The Personal God; Sat-Chit-Ananda; not this, not this.
Ramanuja: the soul contracts and expands with Karma.
Ahara-shuddhi: purity of food and purity of thought.
Time, space and causation as the forms through which we see.
Not one who twists texts; the Kula-Guru custom rejected.
Earth or sun at the centre
Dualism and monism as geocentric and heliocentric views of one sky (Copernicus, 1543).
Ramakrishna the living reconciler; the closing verses.

films.title: Father of Mountains
films.lecture: Address of Welcome at Almora and Reply
chapters: The road to Kumaon and the Himalayas.
The Hindi address: one virtuous son, the moon outshining the stars; hope for a Math.
The Himalayas as the dream of his ancestors; the wish to end his days here.
Everything is fraught with fear; renunciation alone makes fearless.
A place of calm for one eternal religion: the perception of the divine within.

films.title: Theory and Practice
films.lecture: Vedic Teaching in Theory and Practice
chapters: A Hindi lecture, then the English Club and its critical hearers.
How one tribe's god grew by conquering others.
Finding no answer outside, India discovered the introspective method.
Soul and God at one; the reporter's account of the hall merging into Spirit.

films.title: Bhakti at Sialkot
films.lecture: Bhakti (Sialkot)
chapters: Kashmir, Murree, Rawalpindi, Jammu; a lecture in Hindi.
Religions differ in form; Bhakti runs through them all.
Shandilya's intense love for God; easier than Jnana or Yoga; Manushya as the being with Manas.
Hatred saps the current; faces differ, and one religion cannot suit all.
Food and caste rules that lost their spirit.
The Ark, the images: steps, not sins.
Worship for wealth, sons or heaven is not Bhakti; the sadhu who makes gold.
Radha and Krishna: love without fear.
The tigress hunting for her cubs; God is love personified; every man the perfect temple.

films.title: The Common Bases of Hinduism
films.lecture: The Common Bases of Hinduism
chapters: The land of five rivers; the Arya Samaj and the Sanatana Dharma Sabha receive him.
Not to find differences, but common ground.
The name should stand for spirituality and dignity.
A giant whose life is in a bird: a nation's life is in its religion.
India's contribution is the search for what does not change.
"Sects must be but sectarianism need not."
The Vedas, God in many forms, cycles, eternal souls, rebirth.
Dualist and monist both affirm the soul's perfection.
Think yourself nothing and nothing you become.
Love your own people, even when they wrong you.
Light the dark room; believe in man first.

films.title: Bhakti at Lahore
films.lecture: Bhakti (Lahore)
chapters: Seeds in the Samhitas and Upanishads, full growth in the Puranas.
The worth of the Puranas lies in lives of devotion.
Vedanta asks for a fearlessness few have.
The ordinary man needs one; the body is the greatest temple.
Images and temples as steps, lower but not wrong.
Keep your own chosen form; respect others'.
Guruism must stop being hereditary; a true Guru transmits.
Mostly superficial; for the one who has renounced.
Serve the poor as God; the receiver is God for that moment.
Love asks nothing, fears nothing, and is God; the mother who faces the lion.

films.title: The Vedanta
films.lecture: The Vedanta
chapters: The search turns from the outer world to the inner; the Upanishads mark the turn.
Upanishads, Vyasa's Sutras and the Gita under every school.
The faint star found by way of a bright one: from dualist worship to Tattvamasi.
One energy, one primal matter, projection and dissolution. Parallel: conservation of energy (Joule, Helmholtz).
Perception as the reaction of Chitta. Parallel: Helmholtz measures nerve conduction, 1850.
The oyster coats the grain of sand: the mind's reaction.
The river keeps its name while its water changes; the Atman does not change.
Every being holds infinite power, only partly shown.
Dualist and Advaitin on the Atman.
No substance, no Creator; the potter and the pot; Advaita's answer.
The knower cannot become an object of knowledge.
The Infinite sees its own face; three stages of understanding.
"Whomsoever you hurt, you hurt yourself." Weakness is the root of evil.
Serve the starving masses; renounce selfishness.
The secret of Advaita; arise, awake.

films.title: Vedantism at Khetri
films.lecture: Vedantism (Khetri)
chapters: The Raja presides; a summary from notes, with no shorthand writer present.
Two environments, two ideals: the outer infinite and the inner.
Dara Shukoh's Persian Upanishads; Schopenhauer, Kant, Deussen, Max Müller.
Ideas fixed in books; the metres; Karma Kanda and Jnana Kanda.
The double and the laughing gods
Egypt and Babylon kept the body's double; the Rig-Veda's gods were friendly.
The hymn of creation; That which exists is One.
Greece put heaven outside; India turned within. Neti, neti.
The Upanishads; Dvaita and Vishishtadvaita as steps to Tattvamasi.
The spirit lost, the externals kept.
Knowledge is finding unity in diversity. Parallel: Mendeleev's periodic table, 1869.

films.title: Teachers, Not Beggars
films.lecture: The Influence of Indian Spiritual Thought in England
chapters: Old Bengali script on temple walls in China and Japan; the Star Theatre meeting.
Miss Noble, Miss Müller, Mrs Besant and others who gave themselves to India.
Faith in oneself before faith in God.
Friendship only between equals: go to England and America as teachers.
The Katha Upanishad; the conversation in a Kashmir village.
Because you have nothing, you will be sincere.

films.title: The Sannyasin Loves Death
films.lecture: Sannyasa: Its Ideal and Practice
chapters: The junior Sannyasins' farewell on the eve of his second voyage west.
Not seeking death, but offering every act in sacrifice.
Gita XIII.13: the whole world is one.
Be Rishis yourselves, standing on your own feet.
Catch the crocodile first; obedient as this plant and this dog.

films.title: What Have I Learnt?
films.lecture: What have I learnt?
chapters: The beauty of the land on the journey to Dacca.
Searching foreign sects, he found the religion he was born in.
Those who attack idolatry unseen, and those who explain rites with science.
Where Rama is, there is no Kama.
Human birth, longing for freedom, the company of the great.
Scripture recited, never realised; the Amalaka fruit in the palm.
Learned, sinless, unselfish: an ocean of mercy without reason.
Without practice, no realisation; beyond heaven itself.

films.title: The Religion We Are Born In
films.lecture: The Religion we are born in
chapters: An open-air meeting in Dacca; the journey from Colombo seen end to end.
It seems to rot before it becomes a tree.
Sects and customs differ; much is shared.
They survive persecution; the Vedas and the Upanishads.
The Rishis discovered, they did not compose. Parallel: gravitation existed before Newton, 1687.
Everyone has the right to the Veda: be a Rishi.
The Atman known as separate from Manas.
To the God of man through Man; image-worship, lowest but not wrong.
The old edifice; the leaking ship we sail together.
Brahmins give up pride of birth; open knowledge to all.
